"At least MCPs can be unit tested. With Skills however, you just selectively append more text to prompt and pray." — concern that Codex Agent Skills are unverifiable compared to MCP tools.
"This is much better than MCP, which also stuffs every session's precious context with potentially irrelevant instructions." — praise for Skills' progressive disclosure over MCP context bloat.

User describes building custom Skills for a proprietary backtesting framework and niche tools like marimo, having a 'deep thinking agent' do upfront research so it doesn't need to be redone every session.
"Skills are not useful for single-shot cases. They are for: cross-team standardization (for LLM generated code), and reliable reusability of existing code/learnings."
User lists practical Skills in use: writing tests, fetching Sentry info, using Playwright (replacing local MCPs), and submitting PRs per team conventions like lint checks and title formats.

"I wouldn't trust a textual instructions to prevent LLMs from dropping a table" — user prefers building an MCP with restricted tools (listTables, getTableSchema, blocked destructive queries) over relying on a Skill's text instructions for DB safety.
